title: CompiledWorkflowConfig
description: The interpreter's (Python) input contract. Produced ONLY by @arcaai/workflow-contract's compiler (Task 5) from a server-validated WorkflowDefinition.graph. Never authored or accepted from a request DTO. See ../README.md for the normative rules that accompany this schema (no SIGNED node, onTimeout never means approved, formatVersion must be refused when unknown, checksum must be verified before execution).

formatVersion.description: Consumers MUST refuse an unknown formatVersion rather than best-effort parse (the UsageOutboxPayload.version precedent).

stages.description: Topological LEVELS, not a linear list. Nodes within one stage have no dependency on each other and MAY run concurrently.

gates.description: Gate nodes lifted OUT of the stage list so the interpreter can find them without walking the graph, and so 'nothing routes around a gate' is checkable against the compiled artifact as well as the source graph.

loops.description: TASK-864 — one entry per `core.loop`, sorted by nodeId; OMITTED when the graph has no loop so every artifact compiled before this field existed stays byte-identical. Each body is a compiled sub-graph `LoopWorkflow` walks once per iteration.

checksum.description: sha256 over canonicalJson (key-sorted, array-order-preserved) of every field above except this one. Consumers MUST verify before executing.

activity.description: A closed set drawn from apps/harness/src/harness/temporal/activities.py's @activity.defn names. No activity here writes SIGNED (§2.7).

timeoutSeconds.description: Already clamped to caps.maxNodeSeconds at compile time.

onError.description: 'degrade' ⇒ produce a MARKED nothing and continue (INV-019, INV-205) — never a silent empty result.

emitsTrajectory.description: Always true for activity nodes (INV-084) — provenance emission is not tenant-disableable.

branchGuards.description: TASK-864 — present only when this node sits behind at least one branch handle of a router (`core.classify`/`core.condition`) or review (`core.humanReview`) node. The interpreter dispatches the node only when one guard's handle was TAKEN; otherwise it is SKIPPED(branch_not_taken). A branch carries no payload, so it is never an input binding.

onTimeout.description: MUST NEVER be a value that means 'approved' (INV-001, INV-147, INV-181). This schema's own normative rule (see README) is the authoritative statement; the `not: APPROVED` constraint here is a mechanical tripwire, not the full guarantee — a reviewer must confirm the actual enum has no synonym for approval.

guardrailProfile.description: GUARDRAIL_PROFILE_KEYS — placement, not permission; the actual clinical-safety enforcement runs at a boundary this field only SELECTS.

documentTemplateRefs.description: DD-2 — WHICH DocumentTemplate version each generation node decodes its output into, pinned at publish. Structurally identical to promptTemplateRefs and a different guarantee: that one pins what the model is TOLD, this one pins the SHAPE it is decoded into, so a tenant publishing a new template version cannot restructure a document a published workflow is already producing. SORTED by nodeId — the artifact is checksummed, so authoring order must not mint a new checksum for a semantically identical graph. An UNPINNED binding is absent, never versionNumber 0.

contextSchemaRefs.description: TASK-890 §3.4 — WHICH context-schema version each node that binds one by REFERENCE was frozen against. A sibling of promptTemplateRefs with the same guarantee: the interpreter validates a run payload against the schema the workflow was PUBLISHED with, never against whatever the tenant has edited since. Additive-optional: absent means no node binds a schema by reference, never 'unknown', so an artifact compiled before the field existed still admits.

guardrail.description: TASK-890 §3.14 — the WORKFLOW-level guardrail opinion, authored on core.trigger and folded with the per-node and per-agent opinions at run time (node > workflow > agent > on). Tri-state BY ABSENCE: omitted means this workflow expresses no opinion, so { enabled: true } is a recorded decision to screen rather than a synonym for absence.

caps.description: Platform caps materialized so the interpreter never reads config at runtime. 'Tenants tighten, never exceed' is applied at COMPILE time — these are the ceilings the clamp used.
